runs.answer: Inflation means prices go up over time. Something that cost $1 last year might cost $1.05 this year. Money can buy a little less than it used to. Why does this happen? Lots of people want to buy things, and sometimes there isn't enough to go around. When that happens, sellers can charge more.

Inflation means prices go up over time. Last year, a candy bar cost one dollar. This year, it might cost one dollar and ten cents. That means your money buys a little less than it used to. Grown-ups watch inflation closely because it changes how much food, toys, and rent cost. When prices rise slowly, things stay steady.
